Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering team finished a quick run of the pilot workload and we have a clearer sense of token volumes and model mix. Before we commit to an initial reserved tier, we need to nail down two questions for procurement and legal:

1) If we sign a committed monthly slab (e.g., 500M tokens/month), how are overage and burst credits handled? Can we define a credit pool that covers short-term spikes without immediate overage charges?

2) We use embeddings heavily for semantic search (about 70% of tokens) and chat for enrichment (30%). Your pricebook shows a "premium" tier for some chat models (higher-context conversational variants). Is the premium applied per model family (chat vs embedding), per endpoint, or per-token only? In other words: can we get a blended per-token effective rate across models, or do premium surcharges always apply separately?

We'd like to put together an SOW that captures committed slabs and an optional burst-credit add-on. I attached a draft usage report and a one-page SOW outline.

Could you share a proposal with: committed slab pricing, overage per-token, optional burst-credit pricing, and how model premiums are itemized? Also please call out any minimum term or termination fee. Procurement looped in legal on CC.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Mehta

Hi Priya — great data, thanks. Short answers up front and then a suggested billing construct below.

1) Burst credits: we can offer a burst pool tied to the committed slab. For example, a 10% burst credit pool at contract start (non-expiring within the term) plus a per-month burst buy rate if you go over the pool. Burst credits are consumed before overage billing triggers.

2) Model premium: premiums are applied per model family and expressed as a multiplier on the base per-token rate for the endpoint. However, we support a blended effective rate as part of a committed deal (we compute expected mix from your usage report and give a single blended per-token price for the slab). Premiums are still shown on invoices for transparency.

Suggested proposal (example for discussion):
- Committed slab: 500M tokens / month at blended $0.0009 per token (based on embed-heavy mix).
- Burst pool: 10% of slab (50M tokens) allocated at start. Additional burst top-ups at $0.0006/token.
- Overage: $0.0012/token after burst pool depletion.
- Premium model surcharge: shown as a multiplier (x1.5) for premium chat models but waived from the blended slab price above. That means the invoice line shows surcharge details but the committed blended line is a single per-token charge.
- Minimum term: 6 months; early termination fee = unpaid committed token value for remainder of term times 25%.

I'll loop Legal for standard T&Cs and attach a short SOW template that maps to billing lines. If that looks close, Laura can run final pricing approvals and Aditya can confirm the billing code for premium models.

Attached: SOW template and a sample invoice that shows both blended and surcharge lines.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
